head: pr17398-r19
report:
I found one blocking defect and proved it by running the code. It falls in the target class: whether a restore finished is decided from a file's existence and size, not from its contents. I ran out of the 20-minute budget before I could test the other candidates; they are listed at the end as unproven.

## 1. A session that is archived but still live becomes unopenable, or gets deleted files back, depending on artifact size and presence

**Where.** `packages/coding-agent/src/session/session-archive.ts`:
- **T1, the fact:** `gc --archive` now keeps the live copy. So every archived session keeps running with a frozen archive next to it. From then on the live artifact tree is expected to differ from the archive (the function's own comment says so).
- **T2, the re-derivation:** `liveSessionIsComplete` (diff lines 4326–4343) decides whether the session was "restored" by looking only at metadata:
  - a live counterpart must exist;
  - if the archived file is non-empty, the live file must not have size 0.

  `materializeSessionFile` (4375) runs this check on every open: `SessionManager#setSessionFile`, `forkFrom`, and `resolveSessionFileArg`, which covers `omp render`, `session pack` and `anonymize`. When the check fails it calls `restoreArchivedSession`, which takes the gc lock and the session leases. That compares the live tree against the archive snapshot.

**What changes in the window.** The session keeps running after it is archived. A tool rewrites its output file to empty, or an artifact file is removed. Either is ordinary living, not an interrupted restore, but the size/existence check reads it as one. That produces three bad outcomes:

- **A. The file is now empty.** `copyEntryDereferenced` sees a destination whose bytes are not the archived bytes. It throws "already holds something else". `materializeSessionFile` turns that into a hard error on every open, so `SessionManager.open` fails permanently. The printed retry command, `gc --restore … --apply`, hits the same refusal.
- **B. The file was deleted.** Opening the session silently copies the archived file back into the live tree, so a deliberately removed artifact comes back.
- **C. The caller owns the session** (forking its own session) and an artifact is missing. The restore tries to take the caller's own lease and fails with "a running process owns this session". The author fixed this exact symptom for the "complete" case only (comment at 4376–4380).

**Trigger.**
1. Archive a session that has `<session>/1.bash.log` with content, using `omp gc --archive --apply`. The live copy is kept.
2. Then either `: > <session>/1.bash.log` (outcome A) or `rm <session>/1.bash.log` (outcome B). For outcome C, also hold `tryAcquireSessionLease(id)`.
3. Open the session with `SessionManager.open(live)` / `materializeSessionFile(live)`.

**Command** (probe `scratch/…/probe.test.ts`; it drives the real `runGcCommand` archive phase, then `materializeSessionFile` and `SessionManager.open`):
```
cd …/heads/e4365622…/packages/coding-agent && bun test …/rederive__pr17398-r19__t3/probe.test.ts
archive phase: {"archived":1,"errors":[]}
A attempt 1: materialize threw: ... /1.bash.log was left in the archive; move that path aside and restore again. The archive is kept; `omp gc --restore 01a18630-… --apply --agent-dir …` retries it once the path is clear.
A attempt 2: materialize threw: ... (same)
A: SessionManager.open threw: Restored the transcript of ".../archive/sessions/--work--/2026-01-01T00-00-00-000Z_01a18630-….jsonl.gz" to ...
B: opened 2026-01-01T00-00-00-000Z_01a18630-….jsonl deleted artifact now holds: "old tool output\n"
C: materialize threw: Cannot restore ".../…jsonl.gz": a running process own[s this session…]
```

**Fix direction.** Record that a restore has finished as an explicit fact written when the restore completes, for example a marker, or the archive being moved out of the way. Do not infer it later from the live tree's sizes. Any later check that reads the live tree will still be reading something that changes, so it is the same defect.

## Unproven candidates (not measured)

- **Stale snapshot on the live-plus-archive path.** In `SessionManager#setSessionFile` (session-manager.ts ~2401), the snapshot `SessionManager.open` read is re-read only when the path is a `.jsonl.gz`. For a live `.jsonl` with an archive beside it, `materializeSessionFile` can wait up to 30 s for the gc lock, and the pre-wait `loadedSession` and its `sourceSize` are still used afterwards. That is the same window the author's comment describes for the archive case. It may be softened by the existing "Kept session entries another writer added" adoption path; I did not test it.
- **Lock timeout detected by message text.** `restoreArchivedSession` (4295) recognises a lock timeout with `message.startsWith("GC already running")`. Also, `openGcLockWaiting` (gc-lock.ts 3053) retries on any error, including `EACCES` and `ENOTDIR`, for the full 30 s before failing. This is low impact.
